story_text.value:
I built DCIM for people who have a personal website and want an easy way to put photos on it. You upload photos from your browser and paste the embed into HTML or Markdown. You can also send someone a link to the album.

You host DCIM in your own Cloudflare account, which gives you 10GB of free storage. Using another S3-compatible bucket is also possible. I know I use the term "self-hosted" loosely here, but the main benefit of such small software is that you can modify it to your liking (customizable software!) and quickly deploy it on Cloudflare for free.

title.value: Show HN: Self-hosted photos app for the Indie Web

story_text.value:
I've build whatislocalhost.com to showcase an app deployed to cloudish.ai -- Why?

Well, I can either buy ads and brain wash people or, I can burn time, tokens and effort creating value for the community, we chose the latter :)

The last year our team at Hal9 has been helping a bunch of founders that vibe-coded apps turn them into real MVPs (Minimum Viable Products) and then real products that scale in usage and revenue. One of the top questions we get was: why can't I just use my Claude Coded app as my website?

Well, technically you can, but as many of you in HN already know, not the best idea. Computers go to sleep, are more likely to get hacked with exposed ports, have slow and unreliable internet, you only have one, and if you are doing heavy work it will slowdown your website.

Therefore, I created https://whatislocalhost.com, which i an interactive explanation into what is localhost / 127.0.0.1 / ::1

Hope this is useful to some, or at least insightful.

title.value: Show HN: What is localhost? An interactive guide

story_text.value:
Hi. I made small project called Zpup. It takes small 3D scene written in JSON and gives back a flat SVG from any angle. There is no JavaScript in the file, so it works in img-tag or README.

I needed 3D for small project at my company, and Zdog make big impression on me. But Zdog has not had a release for several years, so I wanted to make modern version.

One thing works different. Zdog sorts each shape by one point. so small thing on big floor gets covered when you turn it. Zpup compares the shapes that overlap. You can see both in the README.

I wrote it with Claude Code Fable 5.2.

No canvas renderer, no text shape, and it is 0.2 version.

Playground: https://rxolve.github.io/zpup

Feedback is always welcome :)

title.value: Show HN: Zpup – Zdog style 3D scenes in JSON, SVG from any angle

story_text.value:
I have started using multiple models (Claude, Codex, Grok via cursor-agent, Z.ai, Deepseek, Hy4 via OpenCode, agy) etc, and I realized that I not able to identify which commit was made by which model. After looking around and not finding anything, I create a format specification that will let Model self-identify itself. The goal is a higher ranked model can verify the output of other models and suggest changes. It is similar how to a Senior Engineer will review the output of Junior Engineers. As Humans, we know which model is behaving well, and which we can trust more.

My AI based commits have a identification like this.

Add retry backoff to fetch

Model: claude-sonnet-5-5 harness=claude-code effort=high conf=medium

Model: opencode/hy4-flash-free harness=opencode effort=high conf=medium

In using this, I get an intuition what I can expect when I fire off model on a particular task.

title.value: Show HN: Git Hook for Model Identifation

story_text.value:
I made a site for sharing small tools made with AI.

With agents, it is now quick to build a tool that fits your own task. But those tools usually get thrown away after use, and the next person who may needs something similar start again from zero. So I thought maybe if result or process could shared by text or code and this can lead to kind of token sharing economy. Its name is Disposable and compared to "Open source", I named its philosophy to "Open Disposable".

So the principle is "Like open source, without the upkeep. Keep the know-how, rebuild the tool your way". You can share anything you actually used and found useful, with no promise to maintain it. Others can use it as is, or give the spec that comes with it to theur own agent and have it rebuilt.

If you have your own skill, prompt, or program you would like to show others, please share it. If you get stuck while sharing, let me know.

Repo: https://github.com/x-ify/disposable

title.value: Show HN: Disposable – Share small AI-made tools so others can rebuild them

story_text.value:
Solid 2.0 is now ready after five years, and a huge congratulations to Ryan Carniato and the entire Solid team.

I maintain Lily Design System which provides UI/UX components for Svelte, React, Vue, and more. I have just now completed Solid 2.0 components, and I'm seeking alpha testers to try the new tutorial and coach me on what needs fixing and improving.

http://lilydesignsystem.com/tutorials/solid

This Solid 2.0 port is based on the React components with Claude Opus doing the translation, so I expect there will be AI errors along the way. Lily is free open source and I'm working on it for public sector social good purposes. I'm very keen on the new Solid improvements.

Any feedback, suggestions, constructive criticism, and the like, you can use the GitHub repo or email me directly joel@joelparkerhenderson.com.
